target_customer: Semiconductor and chip design engineering teams that need thermal and multiphysics simulation
problem: Physics simulation for chips needs hours of meshing and setup and can run for hours or weeks on costly compute. DeepSim automates setup and uses AI and GPUs to simulate much faster.
business_model: Enterprise engineering software licensing (not confirmed by a source)
product_category: AI physics simulation for chip design (EDA adjacent)

founders.name: Alexander Gabourie
founders.background_notes: YC page cites over a decade of semiconductor industry experience and nanoscale thermal simulation work; employers not named.

founders.name: Fiona Wang
founders.background_notes: Listed as a co-founder on the company website only, not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Cadence Celsius Studio
competitors.what: AI-driven thermal platform for chips, packages, boards and enclosures, combining finite element and CFD
competitors.traction_then: Launched by an established EDA vendor

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi-scale physics solvers accelerated with AI and GPUs require deep domain research; the team holds EE PhDs focused on nanoscale thermal work.

defensibility.rationale: Specialized solver expertise is hard to copy, but large EDA vendors have distribution and similar thermal products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cadence launched Celsius Studio in early 2024; no source shows any incumbent acquiring or copying DeepSim.

market_need_then: AI chip power density made thermal analysis a bottleneck; the YC launch post describes slow, fragile simulation and says the tool was being validated with Intel (company claim).

branding.domain_note: Uses deepsim.io. An unrelated Deepsim Intelligence Technology Inc. uses deepsim.ca.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, technical, benefit focused (speed, scale, productivity).

brand_strength.rationale: Only company and YC pages describe the brand; no independent press about the brand found.

outcome_analysis: DeepSim is an active Summer 2024 company that grew to about seven people. Its edge is PhD level domain depth in thermal simulation for chips, which fits a market with real need, while Cadence and other vendors compete. A February 2026 item links the company to DARPA related work, but funding is not publicly confirmed.
notes: VCBacked (aggregator only) lists a pre-seed of undisclosed amount in Sep 2024 with YC, NSF, Unpopular Ventures and an angel; unverified so no round recorded. Company site shows YC, Lux Capital and DARPA logos as partners without stating relationship. Company site lists Fiona Wang and Mountain View; YC page lists San Francisco and three founders.
